This confirms the issue. The `attrs` list is built from `[x.attrs for x in objs]` where `objs = _all_of_type(args, DataArray)` — only xarray objects contribute to the list. When `x` (the second argument to `where`) is a scalar like `1`, it's not a DataArray, so it doesn't appear in `objs`. The `attrs` list might have only 1 entry (from `cond`) or even 0 entries if all args are scalars except `cond`.

The fix `attrs[1] if len(attrs) > 1 else {}` correctly handles the case where `x` is a scalar by returning an empty dict (no attrs to preserve), while still preserving `x`'s attrs when it is an xarray object.

The fix is a one-line change in `xarray/core/computation.py:1832`: the `keep_attrs` lambda now safely returns `attrs[1]` only when there are enough entries, otherwise returns an empty dict `{}`.
